CHEMISTRY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Chemistry? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Chemistry.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Chemistry.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Chemistry.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Chemistry.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and bases? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and bases.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and bases.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and bases.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and bases.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2.? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Chemistry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain The Atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Ice melting to water

2. A — 100 °C

3. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. D — Producers

5. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Chemistry.

7. B — Glucose and oxygen

8. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and bases.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Introduction to Chemistry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Atom; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
